Consumer Non-Cyclicals: Consumer Non-Cyclicals posted a robust average annual earnings growth of 34.63%, while revenue rose by 10.37% over the past year. This earnings expansion placed the sector tenth among fifteen sectors, and the revenue increase ranked it sixth. [#VC2.SI]Olam Group Ltd[\#VC2.SI] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration within the group, and [#EB5.SI]First Resources Ltd[\#EB5.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. Growth was further supported by Singapore’s high household disposable income and a cultural emphasis on premium food and personal-care products, which boost demand for essential consumer items. In addition, the nation’s focus on food security and its role as a regional distribution hub amplified sales opportunities for companies operating in this space.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector posted a decline in earnings while expanding revenue over the past year. Average annual earnings fell by 8.04%, placing the sector fourteenth out of fifteen sectors for earnings growth, whereas average annual revenue rose by 14.21%, earning a third place ranking for revenue growth. [#51O.SI]MSM International Ltd[\#51O.SI] delivered the strongest earnings increase in the group, and [#5OX.SI]Mary Chia Holdings Ltd[\#5OX.SI] recorded the highest revenue growth. In Singapore, the sector’s performance is shaped by the rebound in local tourism and heightened consumer spending during major festivals, which lift sales for retailers and leisure firms, while higher labor costs and tighter financing for small distributors curb profit expansion. These dynamics explain the contrasting earnings and revenue trends observed.
Transportation & Logistics: Transportation & Logistics recorded modest earnings growth of 1.78% over the past year, placing the sector 13th out of 15 sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at a slightly faster pace of 2.71%, earning a 12th place ranking among the same peer group. Within the sector, [#FQ7.SI]Salt Investments Ltd[\#FQ7.SI] delivered the strongest earnings increase, while [#R14.SI]Eneco Energy Ltd[\#R14.SI] posted the highest revenue growth. Growth in Singapore’s logistics landscape is shaped by the surge in e‑commerce shipments that pressure port handling capacity and by ongoing government initiatives to expand inland freight corridors. At the same time, tighter driver licensing regulations and rising labour costs create sector‑specific headwinds that temper overall performance.
Healthcare: The Healthcare sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 23.13% while its average annual revenue grew by 3.99% over the past year. Among the fifteen SGX sectors, it ranks 11th for earnings growth and 10th for revenue growth, reflecting a stronger boost to profitability than to top‑line sales. The highest yearly earnings expansion came from [#FHH.SI]FHH[\#FHH.SI], whereas [#8YY.SI]Embracing Future Holdings Ltd[\#8YY.SI] delivered the strongest revenue increase. Growth in Singapore’s healthcare space is uniquely driven by the nation’s rapidly aging population, heightened public spending on eldercare services, and expanding government initiatives that support local biotech research and medical tourism. These sector‑specific dynamics help explain why earnings surged more sharply than revenue.
Properties & Real Estate: The Properties & Real Estate sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 87.21%, placing it third among fifteen sectors. Its average annual revenue growth was 12.71%, which ranked fourth for revenue expansion. Within the sector, [#5IC.SI][#5IC.SI]SING Holdings Ltd[\#5IC.SI][\#5IC.SI] recorded the strongest yearly earnings growth and also led in revenue growth. Growth in Singapore’s property market is shaped by the island’s finite land supply, tight government zoning controls, and sustained demand for both residential and commercial space, especially in integrated mixed‑use projects. These market‑specific dynamics have amplified the sector’s earnings surge while moderating revenue gains.
Energy: Energy sector posted a robust earnings expansion, with average annual earnings growth of about 45.7%, placing it seventh among fifteen sectors for earnings growth. Revenue grew at a solid 21.1% pace, the strongest rate among all sectors, earning the top rank for revenue growth. The sector’s performance is driven in part by Singapore’s role as a regional hub for oil refining and LNG bunkering, which has boosted demand for upstream services. Additionally, the country’s strategic location and well‑developed storage facilities have supported higher throughput for energy commodities. Within the sector, [#JFQ.SI]JFQ[\#JFQ.SI] recorded the highest yearly earnings growth, while [#TPED.SI]PTT Exploration Production PCL DRC[\#TPED.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. These dynamics suggest that localized infrastructure and Singapore’s energy‑trade positioning are key contributors to the sector’s strong growth.
Utilities: The Utilities sector posted a striking 47.89% average annual earnings growth, placing it sixth out of fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. In contrast, average annual revenue fell by 5.3%, which ranked the sector at the bottom of the fifteen‑sector revenue growth list. [#5GD.SI]Sunpower Group Ltd[\#5GD.SI] delivered the highest earnings growth within the sector, while [#BEH.SI]China International Holdings Ltd[\#BEH.SI] recorded the strongest revenue growth despite the overall decline. Growth in earnings has been supported by recent regulatory tariff adjustments that lifted rates for essential services, a factor unique to Singapore’s utility market. At the same time, revenue pressure reflects the sector’s heavy exposure to rising fuel import costs and the need for substantial capital investment to meet the government’s renewable‑energy integration targets.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 44.3% over the past year, placing it eighth out of fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. [#CNE.SI]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE.SI] delivered the highest yearly earnings growth in the sector, while [#5EG.SI]Zhongxin Fruit and Juice Ltd[\#5EG.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. These market‑specific factors have helped sustain the strong performance of the sector’s leading companies.
Financial Services: The Financial Services sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 7.96% and a comparable revenue increase of 8.17% over the past year. In the earnings growth ranking among fifteen sectors, it sits in twelfth place, while its revenue growth places it eighth. [#I49.SI]IFS Capital Ltd[\#I49.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion within the sector, and [#K6S.SI]Prudential PLC[\#K6S.SI] recorded the highest revenue growth. Growth has been shaped by Singapore’s tight regulatory framework that encourages capital adequacy and risk management, as well as by the city‑state’s push toward digital banking and wealth‑management services for an increasingly affluent and aging population. These market‑specific dynamics have helped sustain the sector’s modest yet steady expansion.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector posted a sharp contraction in earnings, with an average annual decline of 107.3%. This places the sector at the bottom of the 15 sector ranking for earnings growth. Revenue, by contrast, grew modestly by 3.2% on average, earning the sector the 11th spot out of 15 for revenue growth. [#9VW.SI][#9VW.SI]Spackman Entertainment Group Ltd[\#9VW.SI][\#9VW.SI] recorded the strongest earnings expansion within the sector, and it also led revenue growth. Growth in Singapore’s Communication Services is shaped by the nation’s rigorous content licensing framework and the rapid rollout of high‑speed mobile broadband, which together influence both advertising spend and subscriber acquisition.
Basic Materials: Over the past year the Basic Materials sector posted an extraordinary average earnings increase of approximately 925.94%, placing it first among the fifteen SGX sectors for earnings growth. At the same time, average revenue rose by about 8.38%, which ranks the sector seventh in revenue growth. [#KUO.SI]International Cement Group Ltd[\#KUO.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion within the sector, while [#C8R.SI]Jiutian Chemical Group Ltd[\#C8R.SI] led the revenue surge. Growth in Singapore’s Basic Materials space is shaped by the city-state’s role as a regional hub for construction supplies, the limited domestic supply of raw inputs that drives reliance on imported commodities, and the sensitivity of local demand to infrastructure spending and global commodity price movements.
Infrastructures: Despite modest revenue expansion, the Infrastructures sector posted an extraordinary earnings surge, with average annual earnings growth of roughly 337 percent, placing it second among the fifteen SGX sectors for earnings growth. Revenue, however, grew at a more subdued pace of about 1.8 percent, ranking the sector fourteenth for revenue growth. [#Z74.SI]Singapore Telecommunications Ltd[\#Z74.SI] drove the earnings acceleration, delivering the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, while [#S59.SI]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59.SI] led revenue gains. Additionally, regulatory approvals and government incentives for sustainable infrastructure projects uniquely influence the sector’s growth trajectory. These market‑specific dynamics help explain the stark contrast between earnings and revenue growth in the Infrastructures sector.
REIT: Over the past year the Singapore REIT sector posted an average earnings growth of about 36.7%, placing it ninth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Additionally, the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s stable regulatory framework and the prevailing low-interest-rate environment support REIT financing and investor appetite, further influencing the sector’s growth trajectory.
